title: Differences between state and government
competency: Identify the differences between the state and the government.

keywords.def: An organized political community governed by a single authority.
The operational arm of the state. It makes, enforces and interprets laws.

ideas.name: State and government are not the same

en.text: People often mix up state and government. The state is the whole country; government is only one of its elements. The state is abstract and permanent; government is concrete and temporary. Everyone is a member of the state, but only elected representatives form the government.

screens.title: After an election
screens.ask: After an election, a new government takes office in Ethiopia. Does the State of Ethiopia change?
opts: No, the state stays; only the government changes
screens.after: Governments come and go. The state continues as long as it keeps its sovereignty.

screens.title: 2.5 Differences between state and government
paras: The words state and government are often used as if they mean the same.
The state is the whole country, like the State of Ethiopia.
The government is the apparatus that governs it.
Ethiopia's government has three branches: legislative, executive and judicial.

screens.title: Six differences (1–3)
paras: I. Government is only one element of the state, which also has population, territory and sovereignty.
II. The state is abstract and cannot be seen. Government is concrete: a group of people using state power.
III. The state includes the whole population. Government is a few elected representatives.

screens.title: Six differences (4–6)
paras: IV. Membership of the state is compulsory: everyone is a citizen. Joining a government is voluntary.
V. Every state has the same four elements. Forms of government differ: parliamentary, presidential, democratic, monarchical and more.
VI. The state is permanent. Government is temporary: elections or revolutions change it.

screens.title: Summary table
table: Only one component of the state
Gets its powers from the state
Forms differ from state to state

screens.title: Key words
defs: An organized political community governed by a single authority.
The operational arm of the state. It makes, enforces and interprets laws.

opts: The state is permanent; the government is temporary
The government is permanent; the state is temporary
They are exactly the same thing
screens.ans: The state is permanent; the government is temporary
screens.why: Governments come and go. The state exists indefinitely while it keeps sovereignty.

screens.title: State or government?
items: A few people chosen by the people.
Gets its powers from the state
The state has the original power.
screens.why: State: whole, abstract, permanent. Government: part, concrete, temporary.
screens.clue: Is it about the whole country, or the people who run it?

screens.text: Membership of a government is automatic for every citizen.
screens.why: Government membership is not automatic. People qualify, run for office and get elected.
screens.clue: Who becomes part of the government?

screens.text: Tigist says: "Ethiopia's government is the same as the State of Ethiopia." Which fact shows she is wrong?
opts: Government is only one of the four elements of the state
screens.ans: Government is only one of the four elements of the state
screens.why: The state is population, territory, government and sovereignty. Government is just one part.
screens.clue: How many elements does a state have?

items.text: Which describes a difference between government and state?
opts: The state is abstract; the government is concrete
The government includes the whole population
The state changes after every election
items.ans: The state is abstract; the government is concrete
items.why: This is difference II in the book.
items.clue: Which can be seen: the state or the government?

items.text: How can a person get Ethiopian citizenship? (Recall Unit 1)
opts: By birth to an Ethiopian parent, or by law (naturalization)
items.ans: By birth to an Ethiopian parent, or by law (naturalization)
items.why: Unit 1: citizenship is gained by birth/descent or by law.

test.text: Which is only ONE element of the state?
test.why: Government is one of the four elements.

test.text: The state is concrete and can be seen; the government is abstract.
test.why: It is the other way round.
Everyone is considered a citizen by the state.

test.text: What can change a government but not the state?
test.why: Elections change governments. The state lasts while it keeps sovereignty.

test.text: Two states have the same four elements but different governments. Which difference does this show?
opts: Every state has the same elements, but forms of government vary
test.ans: Every state has the same elements, but forms of government vary

notes.text: The book's table numbers its heading row "1", so the six differences appear as 2–7; the table also leaves out difference III and adds "original power", which the text does not explain. The lesson shows the text's six differences and the table renumbered.
The citizenship check-point recalls Unit 1; the model answer (birth/descent or naturalization) should be checked against Unit 1.
